transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-17
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 57 min
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Evan Lin (Redwood Solutions Eng); Aisha Khan (Saturn Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Saturn Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (Saturn CTO), Mark Duval (Saturn Finance)

Summary (auto): POC will validate cost & performance for Saturn's summary & chat workloads. Primary goal is to understand per-token unit economics under realistic batching and caching, and decide whether Dedicated makes sense versus Hosted with caching.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intros, we got about 55-60 minutes. today's goal is to scope the POC around cost modeling and benchmarks.
00:18 Aisha: thanks, Jordan. quick background — we run a multi-tenant inference layer inside our platform, roughly 3M monthly queries now, mix of short summaries (avg 120 tokens) and interactive agent chat (avg 900 tokens, with KV caches across sessions).
00:35 Jordan: that helps — can you confirm target SLOs for latency and max spend for the POC?
00:42 Aisha: target p95 latency for chat under 600ms and summaries under 200ms; budget for the POC is capped at $25k.
00:52 Priya: noted. For the cost model we'll produce per-token estimates and show Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. important knobs: batching window, max batch size, and prefix/KV cache hit-rate assumptions.
01:05 Tom: on caching — our sessions persist KV caches per user for up to 48 hours. typical cache hit rate around 35%, but some power users are near 70%.
01:20 Evan: good to know. for the POC we'll parameterize cost by three cache scenarios: low 25%, medium 45%, high 70%.
01:32 Jordan: also worth calling out quantization and model variant choices. you mentioned earlier you're open to a 7B quantized model for chat and a faster 2-3B for short summaries?
01:42 Lena: yes that's our thinking — cost sensitivity on summaries is high, chat we can tolerate a bit more latency/quality tradeoff if it saves money.
01:52 Mark: finance question — when you show per-token costs, make sure we can map that to our current spend line items; we want an apples-to-apples comparison.
02:04 Jordan: absolutely, we'll include an itemized per-call and per-1M token breakdown, plus expected tail spend for retries and fallbacks.

03:10 Priya: quick note on measurements — our benchmark harness will capture: tokens in/out, GPU utilization, observed latency distribution, batch sizes, and KV cache effectiveness. we'll run the harness under steady-state QPS and a spike test.
03:28 Aisha: steady-state QPS for us is around 40 req/s for summaries and 12 req/s for chat, with spikes up to 3x during peak.
03:38 Priya: ok we'll simulate 1x and 3x load. for batching knobs: default batching latency cap is 20ms, max batch size 64 for summaries and 32 for chat; we can vary to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
03:56 Tom: how much does batching actually save?
04:02 Evan: rough rule of thumb — with continuous batching you can reduce token GPU-time by 15-30% on average for short requests; savings change with sequence length and kernel efficiency. we'll show modeled ranges.

05:15 Jordan: let's talk per-token estimates now — using Redwood hosted with our curated 7B quantized model and medium cache (45%) and moderate batching (latency cap 20ms), ballpark comes to $0.0009 per input token and $0.0006 per output token, so about $0.0015 per roundtrip token.
05:40 Mark: can you break that down to per-1M tokens?
05:44 Jordan: sure — that's roughly $1,500 per 1M roundtrip tokens in that scenario. with dedicated reserved capacity we often see 30-45% lower unit costs depending on commit size.
05:56 Lena: what's the delta if we push higher batching? say increase latency window to 50ms?
06:02 Priya: increasing batching window to 50ms typically lets batch sizes grow and can drop unit cost another 10-18%, but p95 latency will increase — so depends on SLOs.
06:18 Aisha: our chat p95 cap is 600ms so we might be able to stretch to 50ms batching on the server side.
06:24 Tom: and what about prefix cache assumptions — if we move to high cache (70%), what's the effective cost?
06:30 Evan: at 70% cache hit rate the per-1M token cost can drop to about $900-$1,000 depending on batching. we'll show a table of scenarios.

07:40 Jordan: we also need to quantify engineering time for Private deployment vs Hosted. Private has higher fixed on-boarding and infra setup, and slightly higher per-token cost unless you pair with reserved Dedicated pools.
07:54 Lena: rough estimate from our side — we can commit to a 6-week POC and evaluate if Dedicated makes sense for full roll-out.
08:02 Jordan: perfect. proposed POC scope: week 0 provisioning and data prep, week 1-2 baseline runs (hosted), week 3 dedicated capacity tests + private networking if needed, week 4-5 resilience/spike tests and quality evals, week 6 review and recommendations. does that align?
08:21 Aisha: yes that's aligned.

09:10 Priya: for benchmarks we'll need sample prompts. Aisha, can you provide representative batches: 5000 short summary prompts (avg 120 tokens) and 50 chat sessions with full histories (avg 900 tokens) we can replay?
09:24 Aisha: yes, we'll share those by end of day Thursday (2025-09-18).

10:00 Tom: security questions — for Private we need SSO/SAML integration, KMS support, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. can you confirm Redwood supports those?
10:12 Jordan: yes, Redwood supports SSO/SAML and KMS/HSM integrations, and we can stream audit logs. we'll include relevant docs in the security pack.
10:20 Tom: also data residency — some EU customers require data to stay in region; we may want to test a regional endpoint.
10:26 Jordan: noted; we'll propose a regional deployment option for the POC benchmarks.

11:05 Mark: on cost modeling detail — please include sensitivity to retry rate and model switch fallback (e.g., fallback from 7B down to 3B for cost savings under load).
11:18 Priya: yes we'll include a fallback policy simulation: fallback percentage scenarios at 0%, 10%, 30%.

12:00 Aisha: timeline question — after we run benchmarks, how long until you can give final pricing recommendation?
12:05 Jordan: we'll aim to have the cost model and recommendation within one week after benchmark completion — so roughly by 2025-10-09 if we finish tests by 2025-10-02.

13:00 Evan: practical note — for hosted benchmarks we'll run using Redwood's hosted endpoints with a dedicated test tenant to avoid traffic interference; for Dedicated we'll provision a small reserved pool (2x A100-equivalent) for throughput testing.
13:18 Tom: provisioning lead-time for Dedicated — how long?
13:22 Jordan: typically 1-2 weeks for small reserved pool if capacity is available; we'll surface exact lead times in the POC plan.

15:00 Priya: sample bench metrics we will report back: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, effective per-token cost, batch-size distribution, cache hit rates, and error/retry counts.
15:15 Aisha: good. also include quality/regression checks — a few golden prompts and human-eval results.

17:10 Mark: finance — we want to see an end-to-end cost table that maps to our billing (infrastructure, Redwood fees, reserved commit amortization).
17:22 Jordan: we'll produce that, with amortized reserved cost scenarios (3-month/12-month) and Hosted pay-as-you-go.

19:00 Lena: any compliance gotchas? for Private we might need to run on-prem for a subset of customers; do you support air-gapped deployments?
19:12 Jordan: yes, Redwood Private offers on-prem options for regulated workloads; it's more of a project but feasible — we'll outline scope and estimated eng effort.

21:00 Priya: operational note — when running the tests please tag benchmark runs and provide raw trace logs so we can attribute anomalous latencies to infra or code.
21:12 Tom: will do.

23:00 Jordan: recap — action items: Jordan to share cost model and security pack by 9/19; Priya to set up bench infra and request sample data by 9/24; Saturn to provide sample prompts by 9/18; follow-up call 10/02 to review results. anything to add?
23:22 Aisha: include a short summary slide that we can share with execs — high-level cost delta and recommendation.
23:30 Jordan: we'll add an exec summary slide.

24:00 Lena: thanks everyone. Mark and I will review the draft cost model as soon as it's in.
24:06 Mark: thanks.
24:12 Jordan: thanks all, we'll send notes and the spreadsheet. bye.

End of transcript.
